learn.hook: Two friends, one roti. How do you share it so nobody feels cheated? Make equal parts!
points: A fraction is a part of a whole that is cut into EQUAL parts.
1/2 (one half) means 1 of 2 equal parts. 1/4 (one quarter) means 1 of 4 equal parts.
In 3/4, the bottom number (4) tells how many equal parts the whole has. The top number (3) tells how many parts we take.
2 halves make 1 whole. 4 quarters make 1 whole.
The more equal parts you cut a roti into, the smaller each part is. So 1/4 is smaller than 1/2.

example.q: A chikki bar is broken into 3 equal pieces. Meena eats 2 pieces. What fraction did she eat?
steps: The whole has 3 equal pieces, so the bottom number is 3.
She ate 2 pieces, so the top number is 2.

learn.reallife: We share pizza slices, cut oranges into pieces and fold paper into halves for craft.

games.title: Match the words to the fraction
Equal parts?
items: A cake cut into 2 pieces, one big and one small, shows halves.
1/4 of a roti is bigger than 1/2 of the same roti.
Cutting into 4 parts makes smaller pieces than cutting into 2.
In 3/5, the whole has 5 equal parts.
The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole.

quiz.q: A roti is cut into 4 equal parts. Arjun eats 1 part. What fraction of the roti did he eat?
quiz.explain: The roti has 4 equal parts and Arjun ate 1 of them. That is 1/4.
steps: The roti has 4 equal parts. Arjun eats 1 part.
Fraction = parts eaten / equal parts in all = 1/4.
Not 4/1: the total number of parts goes at the bottom.

quiz.q: A chikki bar is broken into 3 equal pieces. Meena eats 2 of them. What fraction did she eat?
quiz.explain: There are 3 equal pieces and she ate 2. So she ate 2/3.
steps: The bar has 3 equal pieces. Meena eats 2.
1/3 is the part left over, not the part she ate.
quiz.mistake: Gives the part left over (1/3) instead of the part eaten

quiz.q: How many halves make one whole?
quiz.explain: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts. Two halves together make the whole.
steps: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one half is already a whole

quiz.q: Which of these shows halves?
options: A cake cut into one big piece and one small piece
A paper folded into 2 parts that match exactly
An orange cut into 3 equal pieces
A roti torn into 2 pieces of any size
quiz.explain: Halves are 2 EQUAL parts. Only the paper folded so the parts match exactly shows halves.
steps: A big and a small piece, or pieces of any size, are not halves. 3 pieces are thirds.
Only the paper folded into 2 parts that match exactly shows halves.
Answer: A paper folded into 2 parts that match exactly
quiz.mistake: Thinks any 2 pieces are halves, even if they are not equal

quiz.q: A ribbon is cut into 8 equal pieces. Kabir uses 3 pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is left?
quiz.explain: 8 - 3 = 5 pieces are left out of 8. That is 5/8.
quiz.mistake: Gives the fraction used (3/8) instead of the fraction left

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 1/2 of a roti or 1/4 of the same roti?
quiz.explain: Cutting into 2 equal parts gives bigger pieces than cutting into 4. So 1/2 is bigger.
steps: Both are parts of the same roti.
Cutting into 2 parts gives bigger pieces than cutting into 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction

quiz.q: What does the fraction 3/4 mean?
quiz.explain: The whole is cut into 4 equal parts and we take 3 of them.
steps: The bottom number 4: the whole is cut into 4 equal parts.
The top number 3: we take 3 of those parts.
So 3/4 means 3 out of 4 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the parts must be equal

quiz.q: A watermelon is cut into 6 equal slices. Aisha and her brother eat 1 slice each. What fraction of the watermelon did they eat?
quiz.explain: They ate 1 + 1 = 2 slices out of 6 equal slices. That is 2/6.

teach.ask: Gappu broke a biscuit into 2 pieces, one big and one tiny, and called each piece a half. Is that right?
teach.praise: Got it! Halves must be 2 equal parts. Gappu will break the next biscuit fairly!
teach.nudge: Were Gappu's two pieces the same size? Does that matter?

revise.summary: A fraction is a part of a whole cut into EQUAL parts. In 3/4, the bottom number tells how many equal parts the whole has and the top number tells how many we take.
focus: Write the fraction eaten, used or left
Know what the top and bottom numbers mean
Compare 1/2 and 1/4 of the same whole
remember: 1/2 is 1 of 2 equal parts. 1/4 is 1 of 4 equal parts
2 halves make 1 whole. 4 quarters make 1 whole
The more equal parts, the smaller each part: 1/4 is smaller than 1/2
traps: Don't write the numbers upside down (4/1)
Any 2 pieces are not halves; they must be equal
Don't give the part used when the part left is asked

topics.title: Halves and quarters: equal or not?

learn.hook: Two brothers share a chapati. One piece is big, one is small. Is that sharing in halves?
points: Parts are halves or quarters only if they are exactly equal in size.
To check, fold or place one part on the other. If they match, they are equal.
One line through the middle cuts a shape into 2 halves. Two lines crossing in the middle can cut it into 4 quarters.
Two quarters make one half: 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.

example.q: A square paper is folded in half and then in half again. What does each part show, and how many parts make a half?
example.answer: Each part is 1/4; 2 quarters make a half

learn.reallife: When Amma cuts a cake for 4 friends, she cuts through the middle twice so everyone gets a quarter.

games.title: Equal parts?
items: A roti cut into 2 pieces, one bigger, shows halves.
A square cut by both its middle lines gives 4 quarters.
A line near the edge of a rectangle cuts it into halves.
The line must go through the middle.

items.text: To make halves, cut through the ___.

quiz.q: How many quarters make one half?
quiz.explain: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2, so 2 quarters make a half.
steps: A quarter is 1/4 and a half is 1/2.

quiz.q: A bar of chikki is broken into 2 pieces. One is clearly longer. Are they halves?
quiz.explain: Halves are 2 EQUAL parts. Unequal pieces are not halves.
steps: One piece is clearly longer, so the parts are not equal.
So No, they are not halves.
Answer: No, halves must be equal

quiz.q: How can you check that two parts of a paper are equal?
options: Place one on top of the other to see if they match
quiz.explain: If one part fits exactly on the other, they are equal.
steps: Equal parts must be the same size and shape.
Place one part on top of the other.
If they match exactly, they are equal.
Answer: Place one on top of the other to see if they match

quiz.q: Raj draws one line across a square through its middle, from one side to the opposite side. How many equal parts does he get?
quiz.explain: One line through the middle cuts the square into 2 halves.
steps: One line from one side to the opposite side, through the middle, cuts the square once.
One cut makes 2 parts, and through the middle they are equal.
quiz.mistake: Counts the line as a part

quiz.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal parts. Sana eats 2 parts. What part of the pizza is that?
quiz.explain: 2 quarters = 2/4 = 1/2. She ate half.

quiz.q: Which way of cutting a round cake gives 4 equal parts?
options: Two straight cuts crossing at the centre at right angles
Four cuts from the same side
quiz.explain: Two cuts through the centre at right angles give 4 equal parts.
steps: One cut through the centre makes 2 halves.
A second cut through the centre, at right angles, splits each half into 2 equal parts.
So two straight cuts crossing at the centre at right angles give 4 equal parts.
Answer: Two straight cuts crossing at the centre at right angles

quiz.explain: 4 quarters make one whole.
steps: Add the pieces: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4 quarters. The size stays quarters.

quiz.q: Meena has half an orange. Riya has 2 quarters of the same size orange. Who has more?
quiz.explain: 2 quarters = 1 half, so they have the same amount.
steps: So they have the same amount.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2 pieces must be more than 1

teach.ask: Gappu cut a roti into 2 pieces, one big and one small, and calls them halves. Explain what is wrong.
teach.praise: Halves must be equal! I will cut through the middle. And 2 quarters make a half.
teach.nudge: What must be true about halves, and how many quarters make a half?

revise.summary: Parts are halves or quarters only if they are exactly equal in size; check by folding or placing one on the other. Two quarters make one half.
focus: Check whether parts are equal
Cut shapes into halves and quarters
remember: One line through the middle makes 2 halves. Two lines crossing in the middle can make 4 quarters
4 quarters make one whole
traps: 4 quarters do not make a half; 2 quarters do
Unequal pieces are not halves
2 quarters are not more than 1 half; they are the same

topics.title: Many ways to make halves and quarters

learn.hook: Fold a paper sheet in half: long way, short way or corner to corner. All are halves!
points: A rectangle can be cut into halves in different ways: across, along or corner to corner (diagonal).
It can also be cut into quarters in many ways: 4 strips, 4 small rectangles, or 4 triangles using both diagonals.
Equal parts can have different shapes but the same size. A half triangle and a half rectangle of the same sheet are equal.
To match a part to its whole, see how many such parts fit into the whole.

example.q: A sheet is cut corner to corner into 2 triangles. Another sheet of the same size is cut across into 2 rectangles. Is a triangle the same size as a rectangle?
steps: Each triangle is half of the sheet.
Each rectangle is half of the same size sheet.
Halves of equal wholes are equal.
example.answer: Yes, both are halves of the same size sheet

learn.reallife: Sandwiches can be cut into halves as rectangles or triangles. Both give each person a fair half!

games.title: Different shapes, same size?
items: A triangle half and a rectangle half of the same sheet are the same size.
Each is half of the same sheet.
Quarters must always be small squares.
Quarters can be strips, rectangles or triangles.
There is only one way to cut a rectangle into halves.
4 equal strips of a sheet are quarters.
If 3 copies of a piece cover the whole, the piece is a third.

quiz.q: How many different ways shown here cut a rectangle into halves: across the middle, along the middle, corner to corner?
quiz.explain: All three cuts make 2 equal parts, so all 3 are ways to make halves.
steps: Check each cut: across the middle → 2 equal parts. Along the middle → 2 equal parts.
All 3 cuts make halves, so there are 3 ways.

quiz.q: Both diagonals of a rectangular sheet are cut. How many parts, and are they quarters?
options: 4 parts, all quarters of the sheet by size
quiz.explain: The 2 diagonals make 4 triangles. In a rectangle, each triangle has the same area, a quarter.
steps: Two diagonals cross and make 4 triangles.
In a rectangle, these 4 triangles all have the same area.
So there are 4 parts, each a quarter of the sheet by size.
Answer: 4 parts, all quarters of the sheet by size
quiz.mistake: Thinks triangles of different shape cannot be quarters

quiz.q: A paper is cut into 4 equal strips. What fraction is one strip?
quiz.explain: 4 equal strips make quarters. One strip is 1/4.
steps: The paper is cut into 4 equal strips.
One strip is 1 of 4 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Counts the cuts instead of the parts

quiz.q: Ankit's half is a long strip. Bina's half is a triangle. Both come from the same size sheets. Who has more paper?
quiz.explain: Both are halves of equal sheets, so they have the same amount.
steps: Both sheets are the same size.
A half is a half, whatever its shape: strip or triangle.
So they have the same amount of paper.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different shapes mean different sizes

quiz.q: A piece fits exactly 4 times into a sheet. What part of the sheet is the piece?
quiz.explain: 4 equal pieces make the whole, so each is 1/4.
steps: The piece fits exactly 4 times, so 4 such pieces make the whole sheet.
Each piece is 1 of 4 equal parts.
So the piece is 1/4 of the sheet.

quiz.q: A piece fits exactly 2 times into a sheet. What part of the whole is it?
quiz.explain: 2 equal pieces make the whole, so each is 1/2.
steps: The piece fits exactly 2 times, so 2 such pieces make the whole.
Each piece is 1 of 2 equal parts.
So it is 1/2 of the sheet.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a way to cut a square into quarters?
quiz.explain: One diagonal makes only 2 parts: halves, not quarters.
steps: Both diagonals, two middle lines, or 4 equal strips all give 4 equal parts.
One diagonal gives only 2 parts (halves), so it is NOT a way.

quiz.q: A quarter triangle and a quarter strip come from two sheets of the same size. How do they compare?
quiz.explain: Quarters of equal wholes are equal in size, even if their shapes differ.
steps: Both are quarters of sheets of the same size.
Quarters of equal wholes are equal in size.
So they are the same size, even though the shapes differ.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks halves must always look like rectangles. How would you show Gappu other ways?
teach.praise: A triangle can be a half too! Different shapes, same size. Wow!
teach.nudge: Can halves have different shapes, and what must stay the same?

revise.summary: A rectangle can be cut into halves or quarters in many ways. Equal parts can have different shapes but the same size.
focus: Find different ways to cut halves and quarters
Compare parts of different shapes from same-size sheets
Name a part by how many times it fits into the whole
remember: Halves: across, along or corner to corner (diagonal)
Quarters: 4 strips, 4 small rectangles, or 4 triangles using both diagonals
A piece that fits 4 times into the whole is 1/4
traps: Different shapes do not mean different sizes
One diagonal makes halves, not quarters
Write 1/4, not 4, for a piece that fits 4 times

learn.hook: One big cake for 6 friends or for 8 friends. When do you get a bigger slice?
points: When one whole is shared among more people, each share gets smaller.
A unit fraction is 1 of n equal parts: 1/5, 1/6, 1/8, and so on.
It takes n pieces of 1/n to make a whole: 6 pieces of 1/6 make 1.
Shared among 6, each gets 1/6. Shared among 8, each gets 1/8. 1/6 is bigger than 1/8.

example.q: A watermelon is shared equally among 9 children. Another equal watermelon is shared among 11 children. Which children get more?

learn.reallife: At a birthday party, the more friends who come, the thinner each slice of cake!

games.title: How many pieces make a whole?

quiz.q: A cake is shared equally among 6 friends. What fraction does each friend get?
quiz.explain: 1 of 6 equal parts is 1/6.
steps: The cake is shared equally among 6, so it has 6 equal parts.
Each friend gets 1 of the 6 parts.
quiz.mistake: Writes the number of people as the share

quiz.q: Which is bigger: a share when a cake is split among 6, or among 8?
quiz.explain: Fewer people means bigger pieces. 1/6 > 1/8.
steps: Sharing among 6 gives 1/6 each; among 8 gives 1/8 each.
Fewer people sharing means bigger pieces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger share

quiz.q: How many 1/8 pieces make a whole?
quiz.explain: 8 pieces of 1/8 make 8/8 = 1 whole.
steps: Each piece is 1/8, so the whole has 8 such pieces.

quiz.q: Which share is smaller: 1/9 or 1/11 of the same melon?
quiz.explain: Sharing among 11 makes smaller pieces than sharing among 9.
steps: More people sharing the same melon means smaller pieces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 11 is bigger so 1/11 is bigger

quiz.q: A ribbon is cut into 5 equal pieces. What is each piece called?
quiz.explain: 1 of 5 equal parts is 1/5, one-fifth.
steps: The ribbon is cut into 5 equal pieces.
Each piece is 1 of 5 equal parts: 1/5.
quiz.mistake: Does not name the unit fraction

quiz.q: Riya shares 1 mango among herself and 3 friends equally. What fraction does each get?
quiz.explain: Riya + 3 friends = 4 people. Each gets 1/4.

quiz.q: Six friends share a pizza, then two more friends join and it is shared again equally. What happens to each share?
quiz.explain: More people sharing the same whole means smaller shares: from 1/6 to 1/8.
steps: At first, 6 friends share: each gets 1/6.
Then 8 friends share the same pizza: each gets 1/8.
1/8 is less than 1/6, so each share gets smaller.

quiz.q: How many 1/5 pieces are needed to make 1 whole?
quiz.explain: 5 fifths make a whole: 5/5 = 1.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 1/8 is bigger than 1/6 because 8 is bigger than 6. Help Gappu.
teach.praise: More people share the same cake, so each slice is smaller. 1/6 is bigger!
teach.nudge: What happens to each share when more people share the same whole?

revise.summary: When one whole is shared among more people, each share gets smaller. A unit fraction is 1 of n equal parts, and n pieces of 1/n make a whole.
focus: Write the share each person gets
Compare shares like 1/6 and 1/8
Count how many unit pieces make a whole
remember: Unit fraction: 1 of n equal parts, like 1/5, 1/6, 1/8
6 pieces of 1/6 make 1
1/6 is bigger than 1/8
traps: A bigger bottom number does not mean a bigger share
Don't forget to count yourself when sharing with friends
More people sharing means smaller shares, not bigger

topics.title: Adding equal shares and shading fractions

learn.hook: You eat 1/5 of a cake and your sister eats 1/5. Together you ate... 2/5!
points: Equal shares of the same size can be added: 1/5 + 1/5 = 2/5.
Add the top numbers (how many pieces). The bottom number (size of pieces) stays the same.
To shade a fraction like 3/8, cut the shape into 8 equal parts and shade 3 of them.

example.q: A chocolate bar has 6 equal pieces. Asha eats 1 piece, Bunty eats 2 pieces. What fraction did they eat together?

learn.reallife: When you colour a rangoli square into equal parts, you are showing fractions with colours!

items.text: To shade 3/8, cut into ___ equal parts.
To shade 2/5, shade ___ parts out of 5.
A shape with 6 equal parts and 4 shaded shows ___.
If 5 of 10 parts are shaded, then ___ parts are not shaded.

quiz.q: What is 1/5 + 1/5?
quiz.explain: Add the pieces: 1 + 1 = 2. The size stays fifths: 2/5.
steps: Both pieces are fifths, so the size stays fifths.

quiz.explain: 3 pieces of eighths make 3/8.

quiz.q: A rectangle is cut into 10 equal parts. 7 are shaded. What fraction is shaded?
quiz.explain: 7 shaded out of 10 equal parts is 7/10.
steps: The rectangle has 10 equal parts; 7 are shaded.
Fraction shaded = shaded parts / all parts = 7/10.

quiz.q: Kavi wants to shade 2/3 of a strip. How should he do it?
options: Cut into 3 equal parts and shade 2
quiz.explain: The bottom number 3 tells the number of equal parts; the top 2 tells how many to shade.
steps: In 2/3, the bottom number 3 tells how many equal parts to cut.
The top number 2 tells how many parts to shade.
So cut into 3 equal parts and shade 2.
Answer: Cut into 3 equal parts and shade 2

quiz.q: Tanvi eats 2/6 of a pizza and Jai eats 3/6. How much did they eat together?
steps: Both parts are sixths, so the size stays sixths.

quiz.q: A shape has 8 equal parts and 5 are shaded. What fraction is NOT shaded?
quiz.explain: 8 − 5 = 3 parts are not shaded: 3/8.

quiz.q: Hari pours 1/4 of a jug into a glass, then another 1/4 into the same glass. What part of the jug is in the glass?
quiz.explain: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4. The pieces are still quarters, so only the top number adds.
quiz.mistake: Adds the bottom numbers to get 2/8

quiz.q: How many parts of a 5-part strip must be shaded to show 1/5 + 2/5?
quiz.explain: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5, so shade 3 parts.
quiz.mistake: Shades only one of the fractions

teach.ask: Gappu adds 1/5 + 1/5 and gets 2/10. Explain the right way.
teach.praise: Two fifths! The size of the pieces stays the same, I just count how many.
teach.nudge: When you add same-size pieces, which number changes and which stays?

revise.summary: Equal shares of the same size can be added: add the top numbers and keep the bottom number the same. To shade 3/8, cut the shape into 8 equal parts and shade 3.
focus: Add fractions with the same bottom number
Write the shaded and not-shaded fractions
Shade a given fraction
remember: Add the top numbers; the bottom number stays the same
traps: Don't add the bottom numbers: 1/4 + 1/4 is 2/4, not 2/8
Don't swap the top and bottom numbers when shading
Don't give the shaded part when the unshaded part is asked

learn.hook: Line up strips of the same length cut into halves, thirds, quarters, fifths... Which piece is smallest?
points: A fraction kit has strips of the same whole, each cut into a different number of equal parts.
Five 1/5 pieces join to make one whole strip.
The more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each part.
Only compare pieces of the same whole. Half of a small roti may be less than a quarter of a big one!

example.q: Put 1/6, 1/3 and 1/8 in order from biggest to smallest.
steps: 1/3 has the fewest parts, 1/8 the most.

learn.reallife: Measuring cups for cooking come as 1/2 cup, 1/3 cup and 1/4 cup. The 1/4 cup is the smallest!

games.title: Fraction kit facts
items: Cutting into 6 parts makes smaller pieces than 4 parts.
All strips in a fraction kit are the same length when whole.
That is why we can compare pieces.

quiz.q: Which is the biggest piece?
quiz.explain: The fewer parts a whole has, the bigger each part. 1/4 is biggest.
steps: All pieces are 1 part of the same whole.
Fewer parts means bigger pieces: 4 parts is the fewest here.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger piece

quiz.q: How many 1/5 pieces join to make a whole strip?
quiz.explain: 5 fifths make a whole.
steps: Each piece is 1/5 of the strip.

quiz.q: Which is smaller: 1/3 or 1/10 of the same strip?
quiz.explain: A strip cut into 10 parts has smaller pieces than one cut into 3.
steps: One strip is cut into 3 parts, the other into 10.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 10 is bigger so 1/10 is bigger

quiz.q: Which list is in order from smallest to biggest?
quiz.explain: 1/8 is the smallest piece and 1/2 is the biggest.
steps: For 1 part of a whole: more parts means a smaller piece.
1/8 is the smallest, then 1/4, then 1/2 is the biggest.
quiz.mistake: Orders by the bottom numbers only

quiz.q: Which sign is correct? 1/6 ☐ 1/5
quiz.explain: 1/6 is smaller than 1/5 because 6 parts are smaller than 5 parts of the same whole.
steps: 1/6 is 1 of 6 parts; 1/5 is 1 of 5 parts of the same whole.
Cutting into 6 parts makes smaller pieces than cutting into 5.

quiz.q: In a fraction kit, how many 1/8 strips are as long as the whole strip?
quiz.explain: 8 eighths make the whole.
steps: Each 1/8 strip is 1 of 8 equal parts.
So 8 strips are as long as the whole.

quiz.q: Ria cuts one strip into 3 equal parts and another equal strip into 7 equal parts. Which parts are bigger?
quiz.explain: Fewer parts means bigger parts. 1/3 > 1/7.
steps: Both strips are the same size.
Cutting into 3 parts makes bigger pieces than cutting into 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more parts means bigger parts

quiz.q: Which fraction is between 1/3 and 1/5 in size?
quiz.explain: 1/3 > 1/4 > 1/5, so 1/4 is between them.
steps: 1/3 and 1/5: a fraction between them has a bottom number between 3 and 5.
1/8 and 1/6 are smaller than 1/5; 1/2 is bigger than 1/3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction outside the range

teach.ask: Gappu has a fraction kit and asks which piece is bigger, 1/4 or 1/6. Explain.
teach.praise: 1/4 is bigger because the whole is cut into fewer parts!
teach.nudge: What happens to the piece size when the whole is cut into more parts?

revise.summary: A fraction kit has strips of the same whole cut into different numbers of equal parts. The more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each part.
focus: Compare and order unit fractions
Count how many unit pieces make a whole strip
Use < and > with unit fractions
remember: Five 1/5 pieces make one whole strip
Only compare pieces of the same whole
traps: A bigger bottom number does not mean a bigger piece
Don't compare 6 and 5 directly: 1/6 < 1/5
Don't compare fractions of different wholes: half of a small roti may be less than a quarter of a big one

topics.title: Fractions of a group: my flower garden

learn.hook: A garden has 7 flowers: 3 roses and 4 marigolds. What fraction are roses?
points: A fraction can describe part of a group: 3 roses out of 7 flowers = 3/7.
The bottom number is the total number in the group. The top number is how many we are talking about.
In a garden plan, name the fraction for each flower type.
The fractions for all the parts of a group add up to one whole: 3/7 + 4/7 = 7/7 = 1.

example.q: A garden has 10 plants: 5 tulsi, 3 rose and 2 jasmine. What fraction is each type? Do they make a whole?

learn.reallife: In your class, the fraction of children wearing spectacles, or the fraction who like cricket, are fractions of a group!

games.title: Garden of 12 flowers: 6 roses, 4 lilies, 2 sunflowers

items.q: 2 of 8 laddoos are besan: besan fraction

quiz.q: A garden has 3 roses and 4 marigolds. What fraction of the flowers are roses?
quiz.explain: 3 roses out of 3 + 4 = 7 flowers is 3/7.
quiz.mistake: Uses the marigolds as the bottom number

quiz.q: In the same garden (3 roses, 4 marigolds), what fraction are marigolds?
quiz.explain: 4 marigolds out of 7 flowers is 4/7.
quiz.mistake: Puts the roses on the bottom

quiz.q: A garden plan has 9 beds: 2 rose, 3 lily, 4 marigold. What fraction are lily beds?
quiz.explain: 3 lily beds out of 9 is 3/9.

quiz.q: Gita wants a garden of 8 flowers where 5/8 are sunflowers. How many sunflowers should she plant?
quiz.explain: 5/8 of 8 flowers = 5 flowers.
steps: 5/8 of 8 flowers: make 8 equal groups of 1 flower each.

quiz.q: In Gita's 8-flower garden with 5 sunflowers, the rest are roses. What fraction are roses?
quiz.explain: 8 − 5 = 3 roses, so 3/8.

quiz.q: A garden has 4/10 roses and 3/10 lilies. The rest are tulips. What fraction are tulips?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that parts add to one whole

quiz.q: Do 2/6 + 1/6 + 3/6 make one whole?
steps: All are sixths, so add the top numbers: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6.
6/6 = 1, so Yes, they make one whole.

quiz.q: A basket has 12 fruits: 5 apples and the rest bananas. What fraction are bananas?
quiz.explain: 12 − 5 = 7 bananas, so 7/12.

teach.ask: Gappu's garden has 2 roses, 3 lilies and 1 sunflower. Help Gappu write the fractions.
teach.praise: 2/6 roses, 3/6 lilies, 1/6 sunflower, and together they make 6/6, one whole garden!
teach.nudge: What is the total number of flowers, and what do all the fractions add up to?

revise.summary: A fraction can describe part of a group: 3 roses out of 7 flowers is 3/7. The fractions for all the parts of a group add up to one whole.
focus: Write the fraction for each type in a group
Find the fraction of the rest
Check that all parts add to one whole
remember: Bottom: total number in the group. Top: how many we are talking about
traps: Don't use one type as the bottom number; use the total
Don't add the bottom numbers
Don't forget that all the parts of a group add to one whole

topics.title: Dosa toppings: fractions of a whole

learn.hook: One dosa, three toppings! 3/8 with potato, 1/8 with onion, 4/8 with paneer. Hungry yet?
points: Cut a round dosa into equal parts to show fractions of toppings.
Write a fraction for each topping: parts with that topping over total parts.
To make a dosa matching an order like 2/3 and 1/3, cut it into 3 equal parts: 2 parts one topping, 1 part another.
All the toppings together cover the whole dosa: 3/8 + 1/8 + 4/8 = 8/8 = 1.

example.q: An order says: 3/8 potato, 1/8 onion, 4/8 paneer. How many parts of each, and does it cover the whole dosa?
steps: Cut the dosa into 8 equal parts.

learn.reallife: At a dosa stall, a family may order one big dosa with different toppings for different people. Fractions help share it fairly!

quiz.q: A dosa is cut into 4 equal parts. 3 parts have chutney. What fraction has chutney?
quiz.explain: 3 out of 4 equal parts: 3/4.
steps: The dosa has 4 equal parts; 3 have chutney.

quiz.q: An order says 2/3 masala and 1/3 plain. How many equal parts should the dosa be cut into?
quiz.explain: The bottom number is 3, so cut into 3 equal parts.
steps: The bottom number 3 tells the number of equal parts.
So cut the dosa into 3 equal parts.

quiz.q: A dosa has 3/8 potato and 1/8 onion. The rest is paneer. What fraction is paneer?
quiz.explain: 3/8 + 1/8 = 4/8. The whole is 8/8, so paneer is 8/8 − 4/8 = 4/8.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the toppings make a whole

quiz.q: A dosa is cut into 6 equal parts: 1 part cheese, 2 parts onion, 3 parts plain. What fraction is onion?
quiz.explain: 2 out of 6 parts: 2/6.
steps: The dosa has 6 equal parts. Onion is on 2 parts.
Check: cheese 1/6 + onion 2/6 + plain 3/6 = 6/6, the whole dosa.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong number of parts

quiz.q: Which order covers the whole dosa?
quiz.explain: 2/5 + 3/5 = 5/5 = 1 whole. The others are less than a whole.
steps: A whole needs the top and bottom numbers to be equal.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the top numbers

quiz.q: Lata wants 1/4 cheese and 3/4 plain on her dosa. Cut into 4 parts, how many parts are plain?
quiz.explain: 3/4 means 3 of the 4 parts.
steps: The dosa is cut into 4 equal parts.
3/4 plain means 3 of the 4 parts are plain.
So 3 parts are plain (1 part is cheese).

quiz.q: A dosa has 5 equal parts. 2 have ghee. What fraction has NO ghee?
quiz.explain: 5 − 2 = 3 parts without ghee: 3/5.

quiz.q: A dosa is 3/8 potato, 1/8 onion and 4/8 paneer. Which topping covers the most?
quiz.explain: 4/8 is the biggest since all parts are eighths and 4 is the largest top number.
steps: All toppings are in eighths, so compare the top numbers.
4 is the biggest, so paneer (4/8) covers the most.

teach.ask: Gappu's family ordered one dosa: 2/3 masala and 1/3 plain. How should the cook make it?
teach.praise: Cut it into 3 equal parts: 2 masala, 1 plain. Yum!
teach.nudge: How many equal parts does the dosa need, and how many get masala?

revise.summary: Cut a round dosa into equal parts and write a fraction for each topping: parts with that topping over total parts. All the toppings together cover the whole dosa.
focus: Write the fraction for each topping
Cut a dosa to match an order
Find the missing topping fraction
remember: An order of 2/3 and 1/3: cut into 3 equal parts
traps: Cut by the bottom number; don't add 2 + 3
Don't forget that the toppings make a whole
Don't give the part with a topping when the part without it is asked

topics.title: Sharing a group: fractions of a collection

learn.hook: Dadi has 12 laddoos and says half are for you. How many is that? Let's share!
points: To find a fraction of a group, first make equal groups.
Half of 12: make 2 equal groups. Each group has 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
One quarter of 20: make 4 equal groups. Each group has 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
To find 3/4 of 16, find 1/4 first (16 ÷ 4 = 4), then take 3 groups: 3 × 4 = 12.
The bottom number tells how many groups to make. The top number tells how many groups to take.

example.q: Harpreet has 18 pencils. She gives 1/3 of them to Joseph. How many does she give, and how many are left?
steps: 1/3 is one group: she gives 6 pencils.

learn.reallife: Sharing sweets on Diwali, dividing marbles among friends or splitting a bill all use fractions of a group.

items.text: To find 1/3 of a group, make ___ equal groups.

quiz.q: Dadi has 12 laddoos. She gives half of them to Riya. How many laddoos does Riya get?
quiz.explain: Half means 2 equal groups. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 2 instead of dividing by 2

quiz.q: What is one quarter of 20 marbles?
quiz.explain: A quarter means 4 equal groups. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
steps: One quarter of 20 marbles is 5 marbles.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of groups (4) instead of the number in each group

quiz.q: What is 1/3 of 15 mangoes?
quiz.explain: Make 3 equal groups. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 in each group.

quiz.q: What is 3/4 of 16 diyas?
quiz.explain: 1/4 of 16 is 4. 3/4 is three of those groups: 3 × 4 = 12.

quiz.q: Harpreet has 18 pencils. She gives 1/3 of them to Joseph. How many pencils does Harpreet have left?
quiz.explain: 1/3 of 18 is 6, which she gives away. 18 - 6 = 12 are left.
quiz.mistake: Gives the part given away instead of the part left

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹40. He spends 1/4 of it on a kite. How much does the kite cost?
steps: 1/4 of ₹40 means split ₹40 into 4 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Finds half (₹20) instead of a quarter

quiz.q: What is 2/5 of 25 laddoos?
Joseph shares 24 grapes equally among 4 friends. What fraction of the grapes does each friend get?
quiz.explain: Each friend gets 1 of 4 equal shares, so each gets 1/4 of the grapes. (That is 6 grapes.)
steps: The grapes are shared equally among 4 friends: 4 equal shares.
Each friend gets 1 of the 4 shares = 1/4.
(That is 24 ÷ 4 = 6 grapes, but the question asks for the fraction: 1/4.)
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of grapes (6) instead of the fraction

teach.ask: Gappu has 20 seeds and wants to give 1/4 of them to a friend. How many seeds should Gappu give?
teach.praise: Yes! Make 4 equal groups and give 1 group: 5 seeds. Gappu's friend is happy!
teach.nudge: How many equal groups should Gappu make for a quarter?

revise.summary: To find a fraction of a group, first make equal groups. The bottom number tells how many groups to make and the top number tells how many groups to take.
focus: Find half, a quarter and a third of a group
Find fractions like 3/4 or 2/5 of a number
Find how many are left after giving a fraction away
remember: Half of 12: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. One quarter of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5
traps: Don't take away 2 instead of dividing by 2
Don't find only 1/4 and stop when 3/4 is asked
Don't give the part given away when the part left is asked

learn.hook: Half a glass of milk, a quarter of an hour, one-third of a class... fractions are everywhere!
points: To show 1/3 of a set, draw the set in 3 equal groups and circle one group.
To show 1/5 of a set, draw 5 equal groups and circle one.
To split 16 sweets into 4 equal parts, each part has 16 ÷ 4 = 4 sweets.
We use fractions every day: half a litre of milk, quarter past three, half price sale, a third of the class.

steps: Make 3 equal groups of the 12 bangles.

learn.reallife: A cricket match has 2 innings, each half of the match. A pizza in 8 slices shows eighths!

games.title: Is a fraction used here?
items: One-third of the class went on a trip

quiz.q: 16 sweets are split into 4 equal parts. How many sweets in each part?
steps: Split 16 sweets into 4 equal parts: divide.

quiz.q: To show 1/3 of 15 balloons, how many equal groups should you draw?
quiz.explain: The bottom number 3 tells how many equal groups to make.
steps: In 1/3, the bottom number tells how many equal groups to make.
So draw 3 equal groups (5 balloons in each).
quiz.mistake: Uses the number in each group

quiz.q: What is 1/5 of 10 pencils? Show it by grouping.
quiz.explain: 10 pencils in 5 equal groups gives 2 in each group.

quiz.q: Which is a real-life use of a fraction?
options: Buying half a kilogram of tomatoes
quiz.explain: Half a kilogram is 1/2 kg, a fraction.
steps: A fraction is a part of a whole.
Page 20 and 7 birds are whole numbers, so the answer is buying half a kilogram of tomatoes.
Answer: Buying half a kilogram of tomatoes

quiz.q: 'The school bus will come at quarter past 7.' Which fraction is in this sentence?
quiz.explain: Quarter past means 1/4 of an hour, which is 15 minutes, after 7.
steps: Quarter past 7 means 1/4 of an hour after 7.
quiz.mistake: Does not see 'quarter' as a fraction

quiz.q: Mili draws 12 stars and circles 1/3 of them. How many stars are circled?
A class of 30 children: 1/5 come by bus. How many come by bus?
Ravi splits 16 sweets so that his 4 friends get 1/4 each. How many does each friend get?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to show 1/5 of 20 grains on paper. How should Gappu draw it?
teach.praise: 5 equal groups of 4, and I circle one group. 1/5 of 20 is 4!
teach.nudge: How many equal groups do you draw, and how many are in one group?

revise.summary: To show 1/3 of a set, draw it in 3 equal groups and circle one group. We use fractions every day, like half a litre of milk or quarter past three.
focus: Show a fraction of a set by grouping
Find a unit fraction of a number
Spot fractions in everyday life
remember: The bottom number tells how many equal groups to draw
16 sweets in 4 equal parts: 16 ÷ 4 = 4
Quarter past means 1/4 of an hour (15 minutes)
traps: Don't subtract instead of dividing
Don't give the number of groups instead of the number in each group
Don't circle 3 stars for 1/3 of 12; circle 4

learn.hook: Mummy asks for 'half a kilo of tomatoes' and 'a quarter litre of milk'. Fractions help us measure!
points: 1 metre = 100 cm, so 1/2 metre = 50 cm and 1/4 metre = 25 cm.
1 kilogram = 1000 g, so 1/2 kg = 500 g and 1/4 kg = 250 g.
1 litre = 1000 ml, so 1/2 litre = 500 ml and 3/4 litre = 750 ml.
1 hour = 60 minutes, so half an hour = 30 minutes and a quarter of an hour = 15 minutes.
To find 3/4 of a measure, find 1/4 first, then multiply by 3.

example.q: How many centimetres is 3/4 of a metre?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers sell ½ kg of sugar, milkmen pour ½ litre, and tailors cut ¼ metre of lace.

games.title: Match the fraction to the measure

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in half a metre?
quiz.explain: 1 metre = 100 cm. Half of 100 cm is 50 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses 1000 instead of 100 for a metre, or finds a quarter

quiz.q: How many grams is 1/4 kg?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 g for a kilogram (gets 25 g)

quiz.q: Aisha buys 1/2 litre of milk. How many millilitres is that?
quiz.explain: 1 litre = 1000 ml. Half of 1000 ml is 500 ml.

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes.

quiz.q: How many centimetres is 3/4 of a metre?
Meena buys 2 packets of sugar. Each packet is 1/2 kg. How much sugar is that?
quiz.explain: Two halves make one whole. 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg = 1 kg.

quiz.q: Which is heavier: 1/2 kg of rice or 300 g of dal?
quiz.explain: 1/2 kg = 500 g, and 500 g is more than 300 g. So the rice is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Sees 300 is bigger than 1/2 and forgets to change kg to g

quiz.q: Joseph has a 1 m ribbon. He cuts it into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
quiz.explain: Each piece is 1/4 of a metre. 100 cm ÷ 4 = 25 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of pieces as the length

teach.ask: The shopkeeper gave Gappu 500 g of peanuts when Gappu asked for half a kilo. Was Gappu cheated?
teach.praise: Phew! 1 kg is 1000 g, and half of 1000 is 500. The shopkeeper was fair. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many grams are there in 1 kg? What is half of that?

revise.summary: Fractions help us measure: 1/2 metre is 50 cm, 1/2 kg is 500 g, 1/2 litre is 500 ml and half an hour is 30 minutes. To find 3/4 of a measure, find 1/4 first, then multiply by 3.
focus: Change fractions of a metre, kilogram, litre and hour into smaller units
Find 3/4 of a measure
Compare measures after changing units
remember: 1 litre = 1000 ml; 3/4 litre = 750 ml
1 hour = 60 minutes; a quarter of an hour = 15 minutes
traps: Don't use 100 g for a kilogram or 100 ml for a litre
An hour has 60 minutes, not 100
Don't compare kg and g directly: 1/2 kg = 500 g, which is more than 300 g

learn.hook: Fold a paper in half, then in half again. One half is now two quarters. Same paper, new name!
points: Fold a paper into 3 equal parts, then fold in half again. You get 6 parts, and 1/3 = 2/6.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount using a different number of parts.
To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 1/3 = 2/6 (both × 2).

example.q: A paper is folded in half 3 times. How many parts are there, and how many show one half?
steps: Fold 1: 2 parts. Fold 2: 4 parts. Fold 3: 8 parts.
Half the paper is 4 of the 8 parts.

learn.reallife: Half a pizza cut into 4 slices is the same as half a pizza cut into 2 big slices. Same amount, different number of pieces!

games.title: Same amount?
items: Each third folded in half gives 2 sixths.
2/4 is a half, which is bigger than a quarter.

quiz.q: A paper folded into thirds is then folded in half. How many sixths are in one third?
quiz.explain: Each third is split into 2, so 1/3 = 2/6.
steps: Folding into thirds makes 3 parts. Folding in half splits each third into 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the third stays as 1 part

quiz.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
quiz.explain: 4/8: 4 is half of 8.
steps: A fraction equal to 1/2 has a top number that is half the bottom number.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction with a 2 in it

quiz.explain: Each time the bottom doubles, the top doubles: 4 × 2 = 8.
steps: Look at the bottoms: 2, 4, 8, 16 — doubling each time.

quiz.q: What does 'equivalent fractions' mean?
options: Fractions with the same top number
Fractions that name the same amount
Fractions with the same bottom number
quiz.explain: Equivalent fractions show the same amount in different ways.
steps: Equivalent fractions name the same amount, written in different ways.
Answer: Fractions that name the same amount
quiz.mistake: Thinks the numbers must look the same

quiz.q: Which is equivalent to 1/3?
quiz.explain: Multiply top and bottom by 2: 1/3 = 2/6.
steps: Multiply the top and the bottom of 1/3 by 2.
3/6 = 1/2 and 2/3 is bigger, so the answer is 2/6.

quiz.q: Rina folds a paper in half 2 times and colours 2 parts. What fraction is coloured?
quiz.explain: 2 folds make 4 parts. 2 of 4 = 2/4 = 1/2.
steps: Folding in half once makes 2 parts; folding again makes 4 parts.

quiz.explain: 8 is 4 × 2, so the top is 1 × 2 = 2.
steps: Do the same to the top: 1 × 2 = 2.

quiz.q: Which pair is NOT equivalent?
quiz.explain: 3/6 is a half, but 1/3 is less than a half. So they are not equal.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 2/4 is bigger than 1/2 because it has bigger numbers. Show Gappu with paper folding.
teach.praise: I folded my paper and 2 quarters cover the same as 1 half! They are equivalent.
teach.nudge: What do you see when you fold a half in half again?

revise.summary: Equivalent fractions name the same amount using a different number of parts. To make one, multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
focus: Find equivalent fractions by folding
Fill the missing number in equivalent fractions
Spot pairs that are not equivalent
traps: Don't multiply only the bottom number
Don't add 2 each time; double both numbers
1/3 and 3/6 are not equivalent: 3/6 is a half

learn.hook: A fraction chart lines up halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, eighths and tenths. It is a map of fractions!
points: A fraction chart shows the same whole as rows of 1/2s, 1/3s, 1/4s, 1/6s, 1/8s and 1/10s.
Two 1/4s cover 1/2. Two 1/8s cover 1/4. Ten 1/10s make a whole.
Use the chart to compare: 2/3 is longer than 1/2, so 2/3 > 1/2.
Check if two combinations are equal: three 1/6s = 1/2 but two 1/8s = 1/4, so they are not equal.
Smaller pieces can combine into a bigger piece: two 1/6s make 1/3; two 1/10s make 1/5.

example.q: Are three 1/6 pieces equal to two 1/8 pieces?

learn.reallife: When sharing laddoos cut into halves and quarters, a fraction chart helps check that everyone gets the same amount.

quiz.q: How many 1/4 pieces make 1/2?
quiz.explain: On the chart, two quarters cover one half.
steps: On the fraction chart, put quarters under the half.

quiz.q: How many 1/8 pieces make 1/4?
quiz.explain: Two eighths cover one quarter.
steps: Two eighths fit under one quarter.

quiz.q: How many 1/10 pieces make a whole?
quiz.explain: Ten tenths make one whole.
steps: Each tenth is 1 of 10 equal parts.

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 2/3 or 1/2?
quiz.explain: On the chart, 2/3 reaches further than 1/2.
steps: 2/3 = 1/3 + 1/3. On the chart, it reaches past the half mark.

quiz.q: Is three 1/6s the same as two 1/8s?
quiz.explain: Three 1/6s = 1/2 and two 1/8s = 1/4. 1/2 is more.
steps: 1/2 is more than 1/4, so three 1/6s is more.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the number of pieces

quiz.q: Which smaller pieces combine to make exactly 1/3?
quiz.mistake: Picks pieces that do not fit

quiz.q: How many 1/8 pieces make 1/2?
quiz.explain: Two 1/8s make 1/4, and two 1/4s make 1/2. So 4 eighths make a half.

quiz.q: Which is equal to 1 whole?
quiz.explain: 6 sixths = 6/6 = 1 whole.
steps: A whole needs the number of pieces to equal the bottom number.
Seven 1/8s = 7/8; three 1/4s = 3/4; five 1/6s = 5/6: all less than 1.
quiz.mistake: Does not check that pieces fill the whole

teach.ask: Gappu has three 1/6 pieces and Bubbly has two 1/8 pieces. Gappu says they are equal. Use a fraction chart to check.
teach.praise: Three sixths cover a half, but two eighths cover only a quarter. Mine is more!
teach.nudge: What do three 1/6s cover on the chart, and what do two 1/8s cover?

revise.summary: A fraction chart shows the same whole as rows of halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, eighths and tenths. Use it to compare fractions and check if combinations are equal.
focus: Find how many smaller pieces make a bigger piece
Compare fractions using the chart
Check if two combinations are equal
remember: Two 1/4s cover 1/2. Two 1/8s cover 1/4. Ten 1/10s make a whole
Two 1/6s make 1/3; two 1/10s make 1/5
traps: 4 quarters do not make a half; 2 do
Don't compare only the number of pieces: three 1/6s = 1/2 but two 1/8s = 1/4
2 eighths make a quarter, not a half

learn.hook: Riya says her shape is 1/4 shaded. But are the parts equal? Let's be fraction detectives!
points: Before naming a fraction, check that the shape is cut into EQUAL parts.
Write the fraction as shaded parts over total equal parts.
If a claim like 'this is 1/4' is wrong because parts are unequal, add lines to make equal parts, then count again.
To shade a fraction, divide the shape into the number of equal parts on the bottom, then shade the top number of parts.

example.q: A square is cut into 2 equal rectangles. One rectangle is cut into 2 equal halves and one of those is shaded. Riya says 1/3 is shaded. Is she right?
steps: The square has 3 pieces, but they are not equal.
Cut the other rectangle in half too: now 4 equal parts.

learn.reallife: When you colour a chocolate bar picture in your notebook, check the pieces are equal before writing the fraction!

games.title: Detective check
items: A square split into 4 equal triangles with 1 shaded shows 1/4.
A shape split into 3 unequal parts with 1 shaded always shows 1/3.
To show 3/5, divide into 5 equal parts and shade 3.
A circle with 8 equal slices and 6 shaded shows 6/8.
Adding lines can turn unequal parts into equal ones.
Splitting the bigger parts makes them match.

quiz.q: A square is cut into 9 equal small squares. 4 are coloured. What fraction is coloured?
quiz.explain: 4 coloured out of 9 equal parts: 4/9.
steps: The square has 9 equal parts; 4 are coloured.

quiz.q: A rectangle has 3 parts: one big half and two small quarters. One quarter is shaded. What fraction is shaded?
quiz.explain: The parts are not equal. Split the half into 2 quarters: 4 equal parts, 1 shaded = 1/4.
steps: The parts are not equal, so first make equal parts.
Split the big half into 2 quarters: now 4 equal quarters.

quiz.q: To show 5/8 of a circle, what should you do?
options: Cut into 5 equal parts and shade 8
Cut into 8 equal parts and shade 5
quiz.explain: Bottom number 8 gives the equal parts; top number 5 gives how many to shade.
steps: In 5/8, the bottom number 8 gives the number of equal parts.
The top number 5 gives how many to shade.
So cut into 8 equal parts and shade 5.
Answer: Cut into 8 equal parts and shade 5

quiz.q: Rohan says a shape cut into 4 unequal parts with 1 shaded shows 1/4. What is wrong?
quiz.explain: Fractions need equal parts. Unequal parts cannot show 1/4.
steps: A fraction like 1/4 needs 4 EQUAL parts.
So the shading does not show 1/4: the parts are not equal.
Answer: The parts are not equal
quiz.mistake: Ignores the size of the parts

quiz.q: A strip has 10 equal parts. 3 are red and 2 are blue. What fraction is coloured?
quiz.explain: 3 + 2 = 5 coloured parts out of 10: 5/10.

quiz.q: A hexagon is split into 6 equal triangles. 2 are shaded. What fraction is NOT shaded?
quiz.explain: 6 − 2 = 4 not shaded: 4/6.
steps: The hexagon has 6 equal triangles; 2 are shaded.

quiz.q: How should you divide a square to shade 1/4 of it?
quiz.explain: 1/4 means 1 of 4 equal parts.
steps: So divide the square into 4 equal parts.

quiz.q: A circle has 12 equal parts. 9 are shaded. What fraction is shaded?
quiz.explain: 9 of 12 equal parts: 9/12.
steps: The circle has 12 equal parts; 9 are shaded.

teach.ask: Gappu coloured 1 piece of a shape with 3 unequal pieces and wrote 1/3. Help Gappu fix it.
teach.praise: First make the parts equal by adding lines, then count. Now my fraction is right!
teach.nudge: Are the pieces equal? What could you do to make them equal?

revise.summary: Before naming a fraction, check the shape is cut into EQUAL parts, then write shaded parts over total equal parts. If parts are unequal, add lines to make equal parts and count again.
focus: Write the shaded or unshaded fraction
Fix wrong claims when parts are unequal
Shade a given fraction
remember: Fraction = shaded parts over total equal parts
To shade a fraction: divide into the bottom number of equal parts, shade the top number
traps: Don't count unequal parts
Don't swap the top and bottom numbers
Count every colour that is shaded, not just one
